name: Sawgrass
description: Wetland stabilization intelligence dominating the Everglades through dense rhizome mat formation. Flexible blade architecture dissipates flood energy while maintaining structural integrity. Rapid post-burn regeneration from protected underground meristems integrates fire as a renewal mechanism. Root-zone nutrient sequestration builds soil through organic matter accumulation over millennia.

core_attributes.pattern: rhizome mat stabilization, flood resilience, fire-cycle integration, soil building

scope.definition: Flood tolerance efficiency of Cladium jamaicense — fraction of metabolic function maintained during 6-month continuous inundation (Everglades hydroperiod), compared to 100% at field capacity.

evidence.source: Lorenzen et al. (2001) 'Physiological responses of sawgrass to flooding and drought', Estuarine, Coastal and Shelf Science 52:265-279; Davis & Ogden (1994) 'Everglades: The Ecosystem and Its Restoration', St. Lucie Press.
cross_domain_examples: sawgrass maintains 0.85-0.93 of aerobic metabolism under 6-month inundation via aerenchyma oxygen channels
aerenchyma tissue: interconnected air channels delivering O2 to roots at 1.5 m depth
mangrove pneumatophores: analogous aerial root O2 delivery system for anoxic sediment respiration

scope.falsifiability: If aerenchyma-blocked sawgrass shows metabolic rates identical to intact plants during flooding, aerenchyma is not the flood-tolerance mechanism.
scope.measurement_limits: Flood tolerance optimized for slow-moving shallow water — fast-flowing floods (hurricane storm surge) cause physical damage unrelated to metabolic tolerance. Salt intrusion during drought reduces tolerance.
